x: Parliamentary committees are a main way for Parliament to control the administration, doing the detailed, complex scrutiny the whole House has no time for. The other options describe single committees.
t: Recall why Parliament works through committees.

x: Both are true: standing committees are permanent and continuous, and their membership is renewed every year or periodically. Renewal does not explain permanence, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether renewing members explains a committee's permanence.

x: There are 24 Department-Related Standing Committees: 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha, about 2:1. The figure of 22 (15 + 7) belongs to the PAC.
t: Recall the 16 + 8 split of DRSCs.

x: The PAC has 22 members, the Estimates Committee 30, the Public Undertakings Committee 22, and there are 24 DRSCs, so the answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Note that two committees share the figure 22.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. The 15 + 7 split belongs to the PAC and the Public Undertakings Committee.
t: Discriminate the Lok Sabha-only Estimates Committee from the joint committees.

x: Both are true: the PAC examines CAG audit reports, and the Public Undertakings Committee examines CAG reports on PSUs. One committee's work does not explain the other's, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a second committee's work explains the first's.

x: Both are true: members of the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees are elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote, for one year.
t: Recall the election method and term of the financial committees.

x: The Assurances Committee tracks Ministers' promises, the Petitions Committee examines petitions, the Business Advisory Committee sets the timetable, and the Rules Committee proposes rule changes. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.

x: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first set up as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000, and made permanent in 2015.
t: Discriminate the 2000 start from the 2015 permanent status.

x: A is true: the Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015. B is false because it cannot take up matters pending in court.
t: Recall the Ethics Committee's bar on matters before the courts.

x: Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, Nehru the Union Constitution Committee, Patel the Provincial Constitution Committee, and Kripalani the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Pair Nehru with the Union committees and Patel with the provincial ones.

x: Both are true: Nehru chaired the Union Constitution and Union Powers Committees, which dealt with the Union's structure and the division of legislative power. Their subjects do not explain why Nehru chaired them, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a committee's subject explains who chaired it.

x: All three are correct: H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee, Rajendra Prasad the Rules of Procedure Committee, and K.M. Munshi the Order of Business Committee.
t: Recall each Constituent Assembly committee's chairman.

x: The Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag, under Rajendra Prasad, was set up on 23 June 1947. 16 May 2000 is the Ethics Committee's date.
t: Discriminate between the committee dates.

x: P.C. Chacko chaired the 2G spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee set up in 2011.
t: Recall who chaired the 2G JPC.

x: All five bar Ministers: the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees, the Subordinate Legislation Committee and the Petitions Committee. These committees scrutinise the government, so Ministers are kept out.
t: Remember that scrutiny committees exclude Ministers.

x: The Subordinate Legislation Committee checks delegated rules, the Petitions Committee examines petitions, the Business Advisory Committee sets the timetable, and the Order of Business Committee framed the daily agenda. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.

x: Option C is incorrect: B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan were original members of the Drafting Committee, and N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari replaced them. The committee had seven members under Ambedkar.
t: Check who replaced whom.

x: Both are true: an ad-hoc committee ends when it submits its report, and consultative committees are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
t: Discriminate ad-hoc committees from consultative committees.

x: I and II are correct: the Speaker appoints the Estimates Committee Chairman from the ruling party, and the PAC Chairman from the Opposition since 1967. III is false because that convention applies only to the PAC.
t: Discriminate which committee has an Opposition Chairman.

x: The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee, with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.
t: Recall the 30-member committee.

x: Option B is incorrect: Ministers cannot be members of the Petitions Committee. It has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
t: Remember that scrutiny committees exclude Ministers.

x: Both are true: the Subordinate Legislation Committee has 15 members in each House, and Ministers cannot sit on it. Barring Ministers does not explain its size, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a membership bar explains a committee's size.

x: The Steering Committee guided the Assembly's business, the Order of Business Committee framed the daily agenda, the Rules Committee framed procedure, and the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee drafted Part III. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.

x: Three: Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure, Steering and National Flag Committees. K.M. Munshi chaired the Order of Business Committee.
t: Find the committee chaired by K.M. Munshi.

x: Both are true: the 2G JPC (2011) was an ad-hoc joint committee of 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members. Its membership does not explain its ad-hoc nature, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether membership explains being ad-hoc.

x: I, II and III are correct: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee, Kripalani the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee and H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee. IV is false because Patel, not Nehru, chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee.
t: Pair Nehru with the Union committees and Patel with the provincial ones.

x: Three are correct: standing committees are permanent, and ad-hoc committees are temporary and set up for a specific task. Statement 4 is false because consultative committees are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.
t: Discriminate consultative committees from parliamentary committees.

x: The Assurances Committee tracks Ministers' promises, the Rules Committee proposes rule changes, the Petitions Committee examines petitions, and the Subordinate Legislation Committee checks delegated rules. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.

x: A is true: the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs sets up consultative committees. B is false because, unlike standing committees, they are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.
t: Discriminate consultative committees from parliamentary committees.

x: I and II are correct: consultative committees bring together MPs for particular ministries or zones and are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. III is false because they are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.
t: Discriminate consultative committees from parliamentary committees.

x: Parliamentary committees are either standing or ad-hoc. Financial committees and DRSCs are standing committees, and inquiry committees are ad-hoc. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Classify each committee as standing or ad-hoc.

x: The PAC examines appropriation accounts and waste, the Estimates Committee examines budget estimates and suggests economies, and the Public Undertakings Committee examines PSU accounts. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate before-the-event (Estimates) from after-the-event (PAC) scrutiny.

x: Both are true: the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee oversees both the moral and the ethical conduct of members.
t: Recall what the Ethics Committee oversees.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Provincial Constitution Committee framed the provinces' structure, the Advisory Committee was the parent body, and the Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards. IV is false because it gives that work to the wrong committee.
t: Match each committee to its subject.
